basics.name: Jason (Weifeng) Wang
basics.label: Computer Science & Cognitive Psychology Researcher | AI Engineer
basics.summary: Undergraduate researcher and software engineer at Franklin & Marshall College studying Computer Science and Cognitive Psychology. Co-founder and Lead AI Engineer at Certiferox, engineering retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and psychometric systems. Passionate about AI agents, cognitive workload modeling, and carbon-negative web architectures.

work.name: Certiferox
work.summary: Architected and deployed enterprise recommendation and psychometric modeling engines using frontier LLMs and RAG workflows.
highlights: Engineered Verisona AI through production RAG implementations, optimizing token efficiency and retrieval precision.
Transformed high-dimensional, unstructured open-source datasets into actionable deterministic intelligence.
Designed vector indexing and semantic reranking pipelines for scalable inference.

work.name: Franklin & Marshall College — Department of Computer Science
work.summary: Assisting undergraduate students in Java, object-oriented design, algorithmic complexity, and data structures.
highlights: Mentoring students through recursion, linked data structures, trees, sorting, and algorithmic analysis.
Leading interactive code review and debugging walkthroughs in weekly laboratory sessions.

work.name: Franklin & Marshall College — Office of Community
work.summary: Coordinating leadership initiatives, survey data pipelines, and visual ontologies for campus community programs.
highlights: Designed and maintained deterministic data collection workflows to track inclusive engagement metrics.
Orchestrated cross-functional communication and community logistics.

work.name: CHC Hardware Club
work.summary: Founded and led the premier student computer hardware and architecture society at WHBC.
highlights: Organized hands-on PC assembly clinics, thermal dissipation teardowns, and hardware diagnostic workshops.
Designed and launched the club's static responsive portal.

work.name: WHBC Student Academic Committee

highlights: Coached lower-form students in computational logic and competitive informatics contest prep.
